tells: 1. The laugh doesn't build: across 1.0 s only the woman in the white cardigan reacts (hand to mouth at t=12.6–13.0). The pink-jacket man, teal-hoodie man, purple-top woman and grey-top blonde keep neutral listening faces, so no line seems to have landed (club-5-strip.png, all six frames, front table row)

2. The wide and the held frame are nearly identical: the same heads, hands-on-table poses and gaze directions, with only small head tilts. Read as a crowd, it is frozen, and every front-row sitter has the same posture, forearms on the table and hands clasped by the candle (club-1-wide.png vs club-6-held.png, front row centre)

3. The blonde behind on the left has a broken neck and head: the head is yawed sideways on a stretched, flat-shaded neck that comes out of the collar at the wrong angle, and the face is mid-blink and squashed (club-4-face.png, left third)

4. The face close shows low-poly background bodies: faceted shoulders and a pale-green flat-shaded slab behind the woman's shoulder, and hard polygon edges on the jackets, which reads as a game LOD and not as defocus (club-4-face.png, centre-left and right background)

5. The back of the house is a wall of identical standing silhouettes with no seats, and everyone faces the camera at the same angle. The bar-sign figure is a flat cut-out against the light (club-1-wide.png, rows behind the tables and the bar-sign area top centre)

1. Rows behind the front row hover: the bodies stand upright at seat height with no visible seat, lap or bent legs, like paper dolls stacked on risers. Arms hang straight down and heads are at standing height (theatre-1-wide.png, rows 2–3 centre; theatre-2-mid.png, second row)

2. Every front-row sitter has the same rigid pose: the back pressed upright, knees together, hands on the thighs, and the shoulders squared to the camera. No one slumps, leans on an armrest or crosses their legs (theatre-1-wide.png and theatre-6-held.png, front row)

3. The face close shows game-LOD geometry: faceted, flat-shaded shoulder and arm chunks with a hard pink triangle at the left elbow, a polygonal jacket at the right, and a disembodied pale arm behind her head (theatre-4-face.png, left and right thirds)

4. The back rows read as flat black cut-outs of identical silhouettes in a grid with no seats, and a blue specular glint sits on random silhouettes. Depth falls off a cliff, not a falloff (theatre-2-mid.png and theatre-3-mid.png, top half)

5. The laugh build is uneven but plausible: the front row opens their mouths between t=12.6 and 13.0, but the back rows never change, and the open-mouth laugh shape repeats between the bun blonde and the teal-top blonde, a duplicated character two seats apart (theatre-5-strip.png, front row; theatre-3-mid.png, centre-right)

1. The wide is crammed: front-row knees and shins interpenetrate the neighbour's legs, and the second row's torsos sit inside the front row's shoulders. Everyone sits at the same height, so the room reads as a stacked pile, not seats (openmic-1-wide.png, front two rows centre)

2. The face close has a hair-card mess: a striated, aliased fringe of hair cards behind the yellow-shirt man's head, and a pale floating hand that clips through the blonde's jacket (openmic-4-face.png, top-centre behind the head; right side at about x=1150, y=580)
3. The afro man's head has a hairline seam, a thin vertical line through the hair mesh, and a hair-cap edge floating above the scalp (openmic-2-mid.png, about x=300, y=240)

4. The expressions ramp too fast and in lockstep: the green-top woman and the black-hoodie woman both go to the same wide open-mouth laugh in the same 0.2 s (t=12.6). The yellow-shirt man stays dead neutral, with fixed eyes on the same point, through the whole strip (openmic-5-strip.png, centre pair and yellow shirt)

5. The light is flat and uniform: everyone has the same warm front fill and no stage spill from one side, and the back-row faces are as bright as the front, so the stage look is lost and depth separation is weak. A bright beige door slab at the left reads as an untextured box (openmic-1-wide.png, crowd and left wall)
